newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen Daschle-no activity until chem. arms vote.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen Daschle-no activity until chem. arms vote.

text.p: Senate Democrat Leader Tom Daschle Tuesday advocated holding up all non-emergency activity in the Senate until the chemical weapons ban treaty is brought to the floor for a vote.
"I believe that we ought to be putting as much pressure on our Republican colleagues as we can to ratify this treaty by a date certain," Daschle of South Dakota told reporters.
"So it is my view that we ought to hold up any activity, any legislation, until we can live up to the responsibilities laid out in the chemical treaty," he said.
Daschle said he hoped blocking Senate activity would "force an agreement at some point in the not too distant future to bring up the chemical weapons treaty in a timely fashion."

The treaty, signed by 130 countries more than four years ago, bans the development, production, stockpiling, transfer and use of chemical weapons. Critics say it will do nothing to halt illegal activities by so-called "rogue" states.
Democrats warn that time is getting short. Unless the United States ratifies the pact by April 29 it will lose any voice in its implementation.

Asked whether a vote on a motion to proceed with a nuclear waste bill scheduled for later Tuesday would be affected by his wish to block Senate activity, Daschle said while that legislation was not being specifically targeted he believed all non-emergency activity should be held up until the chemical weapons treaty was brought to the floor for action.

"Except in cases of emergencies involving matters that have to be dealt with immediately, I would hope that we could take that approach on any legislation," until the treaty is brought to the Senate floor for a vote, Daschle said.
